stem: A nurse is preparing an oral medication. According to the Open RN medication-administration checklist, when should the medication label be compared with the MAR as part of the three label checks?

options.A: When the medication is removed from the drawer, while it is being prepared, and at the bedside before administration.
options.B: Only after the medication has been administered and documented.
options.C: Three times after administration so the nurse can verify what was already given.
options.D: Only once during preparation if barcode scanning is available.

rationale: Open RN Nursing Skills instructs nurses to compare the medication label with the MAR at least three different times: when the medication is taken out of the drawer, when it is being prepared, and at the bedside before administration. The same source notes that safe medication-administration checks are not eliminated by technology. Therefore A is correct; B, C, and D omit or misplace the required checks.
educational_objective: Identify the three medication-label check points used during medication preparation and administration to reduce medication errors.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf — Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
source_document_title: Nursing Skills, 2nd edition — Chapter 15 Administration of Enteral Medications
source_locator: Chapter 15 > 15.4 Checklist for Oral Medication Administration, steps 4-7: medication label compared with MAR at least three times — taken out of drawer, during preparation, and at bedside before administration
source_claim_supported: The medication label should be checked against the MAR at least three times: when removed from storage/drawer, during preparation, and at the bedside before administration.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: Administer medications and parenteral therapy; Follow safe medication administration practices
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe medication administration
correction_summary: Reclassified the item from Basic Care and Comfort to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies and replaced the generic 'standard nursing fundamentals' citation with an exact NCBI/Open RN 2nd-edition checklist locator. Simplified distractors and removed the misleading phrase 'checking three times with the same person present.'
